summary: Per the authoritative milestone-scoped timing block, 2026.06.367 shows 0 experiment commits since activation, 0 compute-bound experiments, and 0 minutes of measured experiment wall-time; both RTX 3090s sat at 0% utilization, which is correct behaviour when no compute-bound task ran (so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null and GPU idle is NOT a bottleneck). However, the committed .367 changelog window contains real experiment work, so the zero-count is most plausibly a milestone-to-commit attribution/windowing gap in the timing detector — now the 4th consecutive false zero (.363/.365/.366/.367) — rather than a genuinely empty milestone.
bottlenecks_identified: Recurring false zero-count: the milestone-scoped timing detector reports 0 experiment commits since activation for the 4th consecutive milestone (.363/.365/.366/.367), even though the committed changelog window for .367 contains real experiment work. The operational bottleneck is the detector/windowing, not the experiments.

Data-starved retro: with the timing block empty, there is no per-experiment duration to rank, so questions 1-3 (slowest experiments, GPU efficiency, DualGPURunner engagement) cannot be answered from the authoritative data this milestone.

(Not a bottleneck — explicitly cleared) Both GPUs idle at 0% util with 4MB resident is correct because zero compute-bound tasks are present (gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null); per the GPU-idle interpretation rule this is expected behaviour, not flagged.
improvements_suggested: Repair the timing harness's commit detection/windowing: audit the activation-boundary SHA and the experiment-artifact filename match used to scope commits to a milestone; a recurring false zero across four milestones indicates the range query (not the milestone) is wrong.

Add a self-check that diffs the detector's commit count against a direct git-range artifact count and stamps detector_gap_suspected on the retro when they disagree, so an empty timing block is never silently treated as an empty milestone.
Backfill the timing analysis over .363-.367 once the detector is fixed, to recover the per-experiment durations the retros have been unable to report.
Do NOT enforce DualGPURunner this milestone: no compute-bound task and no 2+-model-parallel task are present in the data, so the single-vs-dual-GPU question is not applicable.
Optionally free the 4MB lingering allocation on each GPU so the next compute-bound run starts from a clean 0MB baseline (advisory, not load-bearing).
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the milestone->commit detector/windowing — the same false zero-count has now recurred four milestones running, so each retro is running on empty input and cannot do its job; this is the single change that unblocks all four operational questions.

Add a detector_gap_suspected self-check (detector count vs direct git-range count) so future zero-count retros carry a root-cause breadcrumb instead of silently mis-reading a productive milestone as empty.
Backfill .363-.367 timing once fixed to recover the lost per-experiment duration record and confirm the GPU/DualGPURunner questions retroactively.
meta_reflection: The load-bearing operational signal is that the zero-count is almost certainly an artifact of a broken milestone-scoped commit detector, not an idle loop — the committed .367 record shows real work. Four consecutive false zeros (.363/.365/.366/.367) means the retro tooling itself is the bottleneck worth fixing; until the detector is repaired, each operational retro is forced to run on empty input and cannot answer the questions it exists to answer.
